items.title: ‘Love Trapped’ Podcast Featuring Former ‘Bachelor’ Star Clayton Echard Being Adapted As True-Crime Series For Peacock
items.summary:
Peacock has ordered a four-part true-crime docuseries about Laura Owens, the woman sentenced last month to a month in jail after faking a pregnancy in an attempt to entrap former Bachelor star Clayton Echard. The project carries the working title Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens and is set to premiere next year.

The series adapts the iHeart podcast Love Trapped, hosted by Stephani Young, which launched in September and built a sizable audience chronicling Owens' brief relationship with Echard and her claim that she was pregnant with twins before the story came apart. Echard appeared on season 18 of The Bachelorette and season 26 of The Bachelor.

Deadline reported the order, noting that the docuseries will feature interviews with Echard and his legal team, Owens' mother Jan Black, other men Owens targeted, Young herself, and the online amateur investigators who helped pull the case apart. Owens also speaks about her experience on camera for the first time.

Glass Entertainment Group and Crybaby Media, the two companies behind the podcast, are producing. Nancy Glass, Erin Lee Carr and Keayr Braxton executive produce for Glass Entertainment Group, with Braxton directing, and Danny Passman executive produces for Crybaby Media.

Peacock has not announced a premiere date beyond the 2026 window. The sentence Owens received last month closed the legal chapter of the story; the series is the first time she has addressed it publicly at length.

items.title: Duran Duran’s Roger Taylor Announces Retirement
items.summary:
Roger Taylor, the founding drummer of Duran Duran, has retired from the band. The 66-year-old announced the decision in a statement posted to Duran Duran's website and social accounts, citing a tinnitus diagnosis that has worsened to the point where he can no longer continue. His last performance with the group was at Movistar Arena in Madrid last Friday.

"This is one of the hardest decisions I've ever had to make," Taylor said in the statement. "Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I'll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they've shown us over the years. But the truth is that my tinnitus has been getting steadily worse, and I've reached the point where I must now listen to my body and my doctors."

Taylor framed the timing as a choice to leave on strong footing. He pointed to the band's recently completed UK and European tour, a second headline show at BST Hyde Park, Duran Duran's induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and a return to the studio with Nile Rodgers. "I move on with enormous pride, and with nothing but love for Simon, Nick and John," he wrote.

Stereogum reported the announcement, noting that Taylor joined as Duran Duran's first drummer in 1979 and played on the band's first three albums as they became fixtures of early MTV and one of the defining acts of the new wave era. He left in 1985 after the group's Live Aid performance, worn down by fame and the touring schedule.

Taylor returned in 2001 when Duran Duran reassembled the lineup that made 1982's Rio, a reunion that produced a hugely successful tour and kept him behind the kit for the next two decades. The band has not said whether it will name a replacement.

items.title: Deftones Plot 2027 North American Tour
items.summary:
Deftones have mapped out a North American tour for spring 2027, their first major run announced since last weekend's Día De Los Deftones festival set. The itinerary opens May 5 at Dos Equis Pavilion in Dallas and closes June 20 at RBC Amphitheatre in Toronto.

Knocked Loose and the rock and shoegaze band Julie will open every date on the tour, according to Pitchfork. The pairing puts one of metalcore's most prominent current acts alongside a younger group working a softer, noisier register, which suits a Deftones bill that has long spanned both.

The routing leans heavily on amphitheaters, with stops in San Antonio, Houston, Albuquerque, Phoenix, Wheatland, Concord, Auburn, Ridgefield, Kansas City, St. Louis, Atlanta, Charlotte, Clarkston, Noblesville, Cincinnati, Bristow, Virginia Beach and Camden. Two dates stand out from that pattern: Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles on May 18 and Forest Hills Stadium in Queens on June 17. The band will also play Kilby Block Party in Salt Lake City on May 14.

The run follows Private Music, the album Deftones released in 2025. Tickets for the 2027 dates are being sold through Ticketmaster and resale sites.
